conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee, one of the surgical team members. You're here today for your scheduled gastrostomy tube placement, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. I’ve been having so much nausea and trouble keeping food down. I hope this helps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. This tube will help transition you from TPN to tube feedings, which should be easier on your system. The procedure is done by interventional radiology, and you’ll be back here afterward.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I feel anything during the procedure?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get sedation—fentanyl and Versed—so you’ll be drowsy and comfortable. Your vital signs will be closely watched the whole time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that sounds okay. And the tube goes into my stomach?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, into the gastric remnant—your stomach pouch from the bypass. It’s placed under fluoroscopy, so they can see exactly where it goes. It’s a minimally invasive procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I’ll start feeds right away?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not immediately. We’ll start with clear liquids by mouth tomorrow to make sure you tolerate that. Then, after 24 hours, we’ll begin tube feeds slowly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my PICC line—will that stay in?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll remove it once you’re tolerating tube feeds well. Since you’re on TPN now, we’ll keep it until we’re sure the tube feeding is working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. I’ve been on TPN for a while, but it’s not ideal long-term.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. The goal is to get you off TPN and onto enteral nutrition, which is safer and more natural for your gut.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re back! The procedure went smoothly. The tube is in place, and the chest X-ray confirms it’s positioned correctly in your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. Does it hurt? I feel a little pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Some mild tenderness is normal. We’ll give you pain meds if needed. The site is dressed and secured with sutures. We’ll keep an eye on it for any signs of infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the PICC is still in?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, still in. We’ll continue your TPN and IV pantoprazole for now. Tomorrow, we’ll start you on clear liquids by mouth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling? Any nausea or pain at the tube site?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little sore, but not bad. I had some water last night and kept it down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’ll start advancing your diet today. First, clear liquids, then if you do well, we’ll begin tube feeds this afternoon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What kind of formula will I get through the tube?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re starting with ‘Replete with Fiber’—it’s balanced and includes fiber to help with bowel regularity. It’ll run at 110 mL per hour for 12 hours overnight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I’ll still take my regular meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all your home meds—aripiprazole, citalopram, lamotrigine, lorazepam, nortriptyline, temazepam, and pantoprazole. We’ll switch pantoprazole to oral today since you can swallow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re starting your tube feeds now. We’ll begin slowly and monitor for any nausea or bloating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Should I feel anything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You might feel a little fullness, but not pain. Let us know if you feel nauseous or crampy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well—no nausea, and the feeds are going at goal rate. We’re going to try advancing you to a regular diet tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Really? I haven’t eaten solid food in weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start with small amounts. If you tolerate it, you can eat more. Your nausea has improved, which is a good sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You had a good night—feeds completed, no issues. We removed the PICC line this morning since you’re stable on enteral nutrition.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. I was worried about infections from the line.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Now we focus on your recovery at home. You’ll continue the tube feeds overnight and take pantoprazole daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the pain med?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Oxycodone-acetaminophen as needed. But use it sparingly—your pain is mild, and we want you off opioids quickly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see surgery in two weeks. Also, continue with gastroenterology—they’re managing your cyclic vomiting syndrome with nortriptyline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the tube care at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep the site clean and dry. Wash with soapy water daily. Watch for redness, swelling, or discharge. Call if you have fever or worsening pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And can I shower?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but keep the site dry—use a waterproof cover. No baths or swimming for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll be careful. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll get the discharge papers ready. You’re doing great—tolerating feeds, walking, and pain controlled. You’ll go home with a nurse visit to help with the pump.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’m hopeful this will help me eat better and gain weight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We are too. The goal is improved nutrition and fewer hospital visits. Keep up the good work.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check before discharge. Your labs are stable—hemoglobin, electrolytes, kidney function—all good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s reassuring. And my malnutrition?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: This tube is the key. With consistent feeds, your nutrition should improve over the next few weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll stick to the plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Remember: call if you vomit, can’t keep fluids down, have chest pain, or fever over 101.5.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll see you in follow-up. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The enteral infusion is running smoothly. You’ve reached goal rate. We’re documenting this as part of your discharge process.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It feels normal. I didn’t even notice it started.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s ideal. Means your body is adjusting well. You’re ready for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I feel like I can manage this at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re confident too. Just follow the instructions, and you’ll do well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you soon.
